text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Lassaigne's test, the covalent organic molecules are transformed into ionic compounds.

Statement II: The sodium fusion extract of an organic compound having N and S gives prussian blue colour with $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{Na}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]$

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is true.

In Lassaigne’s test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal. During this fusion, elements present in the covalent organic compound are converted into ionic sodium salts.

For example,

$\text{C, N}\leftarrow ^{\text{Na}}\mathrm{NaCN}$

$\text{S}\leftarrow ^{\text{Na}}\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{S}$

$\text{X}\leftarrow ^{\text{Na}}\mathrm{NaX}$

So, covalent organic molecules are changed into ionic compounds. Hence, Statement I is true.

Statement II is false.

If an organic compound contains both nitrogen and sulphur, then during sodium fusion it generally forms sodium thiocyanate:

$\mathrm{Na}+\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{N}+\mathrm{S}\to \mathrm{NaSCN}$

Sodium thiocyanate gives a blood-red colour with ferric ions due to formation of ferric thiocyanate complex, not Prussian blue.

Prussian blue colour is obtained in the test for nitrogen when sodium cyanide is formed:

$\mathrm{NaCN}+\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}\to \mathrm{Na}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]$

On acidification, it gives Prussian blue.

But for a compound having both N and S together, the characteristic test is blood-red colour due to thiocyanate, not Prussian blue.

So, the correct answer is:

$\text{Option D: Statement I is true but Statement II is false}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
$\mathrm{FeO}_{4}^{2-}\leftarrow ^{+2.0\mathrm{V}}\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\leftarrow ^{0.8\mathrm{V}}\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\leftarrow ^{-0.5\mathrm{V}}\mathrm{Fe}^{0}$

In the above diagram, the standard electrode potentials are given in volts (over the arrow).

The value of $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{FeO}_{4}^{2-}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The oxidation state of Fe is $+6$ in $\mathrm{FeO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$, $+3$ in $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ and $+2$ in $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$, so the two given steps involve $n_{1}=3$ and $n_{2}=1$ electrons, and $\mathrm{FeO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}\to \mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ involves $n=4$.

Electrode potentials are not additive, but $\Delta G^{\circ }=-nFE^{\circ }$ is:

$\Delta G^{\circ }=\Delta G_{1}^{\circ }+\Delta G_{2}^{\circ }\Rightarrow -4FE^{\circ }=-3F(2.0)-1F(0.8)$

$E_{\mathrm{FeO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}/\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}}^{\circ }=\dfrac{3(2.0)+1(0.8)}{4}=\dfrac{6.8}{4}=1.7\text{V}$

The $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}/\mathrm{Fe}$ potential ($-0.5$ V) is not needed.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: $\mathrm{CrCl}_{3}\cdot \mathrm{xNH}_{3}$ can exist as a complex. 0.1 molal aqueous solution of this complex shows a depression in freezing point of $0.558^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. Assuming $100%$ ionisation of this complex and coordination number of Cr is 6 , the complex will be (Given $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}=1.86\mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$i=\dfrac{\Delta T_{f}}{K_{f}m}=\dfrac{0.558}{1.86\times 0.1}=3$

So each formula unit gives 3 particles in solution. With coordination number 6, the options ionise as follows.

(A) $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$: 3 ions.

(B) $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$: 2 ions.

(C) $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}+3\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$: 4 ions.

(D) $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}]$ is a non-electrolyte: 1 particle.

Only (A) gives $i=3$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The major product of the following reaction is : 

$\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{O}\leftarrow _{\text{reflux}}^{\begin{array}{l} \text{excess}\mathrm{HCHO} \\ \text{alkali} \end{array}}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Propanal, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$, has two $α$-hydrogens, while formaldehyde has none and is the more reactive carbonyl acceptor.

In alkali, two successive crossed aldol additions with HCHO replace both $α$-hydrogens by $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ groups, giving 2,2-bis(hydroxymethyl)propanal, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$. With excess HCHO the second addition takes place instead of dehydration, so the unsaturated aldehyde of (A) is not the final product.

This aldehyde has no $α$-hydrogen, so with excess HCHO and alkali it undergoes a crossed Cannizzaro reaction: HCHO is oxidised to formate and the aldehyde is reduced to a primary alcohol.

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}+\mathrm{HCHO}+\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}){}_{3}+\mathrm{HCOO}{}^{-}$


[IMG]

The major product is 2-(hydroxymethyl)-2-methylpropane-1,3-diol, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}){}_{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: The incorrect statement among the following is
options: $\mathrm{SO}_{2}$ can act as an oxidizing agent, but not as a reducing agent.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{PH}_{3}$ shows lower proton affinity than $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$.

Ammonia (NH₃) has a more available lone pair on nitrogen than PH₃ on phosphorus due to smaller size and higher electronegativity. Thus, NH₃ is a stronger base and has a higher proton affinity than PH₃.  

This statement is correct.

$\mathrm{SO}_{2}$ can act as an oxidizing agent, but not as a reducing agent.

Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is quite versatile in redox chemistry. In many reactions, it actually behaves as a reducing agent by being oxidized (e.g., to sulfate, where sulfur goes from +4 to +6 oxidation state). While under some conditions it may act as an oxidizing agent, it is well known and widely used for its reducing properties.  

Hence, the claim that it “cannot act as a reducing agent” is incorrect.

$\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ can dimerise easily.

Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) is known to dimerise to form dinitrogen tetroxide (N₂O₄), especially at lower temperatures.  

This statement is correct.

$\mathrm{PF}_{3}$ exists but $\mathrm{NF}_{5}$ does not.

Phosphorus trifluoride (PF₃) is a known stable compound. In contrast, a compound like nitrogen pentafluoride (NF₅) is not observed, largely due to the limitations of nitrogen’s size and bonding capabilities in forming such a structure.  

This statement is correct.

Based on the analysis, the incorrect statement is:

Option B.

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Fructose does not contain an aldehydic group but still reduces Tollen's reagent

Statement II: In the presence of base, fructose undergoes rearrangement to give glucose.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fructose is a ketohexose; it has no $-\mathrm{CHO}$ group but carries a $-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ ($α$-hydroxy ketone) unit at C-1 and C-2.

In the presence of a base, fructose is converted through an enediol intermediate into an equilibrium mixture containing D-glucose and D-mannose (Lobry de Bruyn–van Ekenstein rearrangement), so Statement II is true.


[IMG]

Tollens' reagent is alkaline, so this rearrangement takes place in the reagent itself; the aldoses formed are oxidised and silver is deposited. Fructose therefore reduces Tollens' reagent without having an aldehyde group, so Statement I is true.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following happens when $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ is added gradually to the solution containing 1 M $\mathrm{A}^{2+}$ and $1\mathrm{M}\mathrm{B}^{3+}$ ions?

Given : $\mathrm{K}_{\text{sp}}[\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}]=9\times 10^{-10}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}]=27\times 10^{-18}$ at 298 K.
options: Both $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ and $\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ do not show precipitation with $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Condition for precipitation $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{ip}}>\mathrm{K}_{\text{sp}}$

For $[\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}]$

$\begin{array}{l} \left [\mathrm{A}^{2+}\right ]\left [\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right ]^{2}>9\times 10^{-10} \\ \left [\mathrm{A}^{+2}\right ]=1\mathrm{M} \\ \Rightarrow \left [\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right ]>3\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{M} \end{array}$

For $[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}]$

$\begin{array}{l} \left [\mathrm{B}^{3+}\right ]\left [\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right ]^{3}>27\times 10^{-18} \\ \left [\mathrm{B}^{3+}\right ]=1\mathrm{M} \\ \Rightarrow \left [\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right ]>3\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{M} \end{array}$

So, $\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ will precipitate before $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: The d-electronic configuration of an octahedral Co (II) complex having magnetic moment of 3.95 BM is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The spin-only moment is $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM; $n=3$ gives $\sqrt{15}=3.87$ BM, closest to 3.95 BM, so the complex has 3 unpaired electrons.

$\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{7}$. In an octahedral field, the high-spin arrangement $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{2}$ has 3 unpaired electrons, while the low-spin arrangement $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1}$ has only 1.


[IMG]

$e^{4}t_{2}^{3}$ is a tetrahedral splitting pattern and $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{0}$ holds only 3 electrons, so neither describes an octahedral $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ complex.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about 900 nm . Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this?

Given : Rydberg constant $\left. \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=10^{5}\mathrm{cm}^{-1},\mathrm{h}=6.6\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{s},\mathrm{c}=3\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine which spectral line of the hydrogen atom suits the wavelength for heat treatment of muscular pain (900 nm), we begin by applying the Rydberg equation:

$\frac{1}{λ}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{Z}^{2}\left (\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right )$

Given:

$λ=900\text{nm}=9\times 10^{-5}\text{cm}$

$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=10^{5}\text{cm}^{-1}$

Hydrogen atom (Z = 1)

We proceed by solving the equation:

$\frac{1}{λ\times \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}$

Substituting the known values:

$\frac{1}{9\times 10^{-5}\text{cm}\times 10^{5}\text{cm}^{-1}}=\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}$

This simplifies to:

$\frac{1}{9}=\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}$

This condition is satisfied when $n_{1}=3$ and $n_{2}=\infty$.

Therefore, the appropriate spectral transition is from $n_{2}=\infty$ to $n_{1}=3$, which corresponds to the Paschen series transition $\infty \to 3$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
Which among the following react with Hinsberg's reagent?

A. 
[IMG]

$\text{C.}\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{NH}_{2}$

D. $\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{3}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$. It reacts only with amines that have an $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ bond, that is, $1^{\circ }$ and $2^{\circ }$ amines, replacing that hydrogen to give a sulphonamide.

A, aniline $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, and C, methylamine $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, are $1^{\circ }$ amines and react.

E, diphenylamine $(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}){}_{2}\mathrm{NH}$, is a $2^{\circ }$ amine and reacts.

B, N,N-dimethylaniline $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, and D, trimethylamine $\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$, are $3^{\circ }$ amines with no $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ and do not react.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

$2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}(\mathrm{g})\to 2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

  
    Sr. No.
    Time/s
    Total pressure/(atm)
  

  
    1
    0
    0.6
  
  
    2
    100
    '$\mathrm{x}$'
  

$\mathrm{x}=$ $__________$ $\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{atm}$ [nearest integer]

Given : Rate constant for the reaction is $4.606\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}}=2\times 4.606\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{S}^{-1} \\ 2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}(\mathrm{g})⟶2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g}) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{llll} P_{i} & 0.6 & 0 & 0 \\ P_{f} & 0.6-P & P & \frac{P}{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} 2\times 4.606\times 10^{-2}=\dfrac{2.303}{100}\log \dfrac{0.6}{0.6-\mathrm{P}} \\ 4=\log _{10}\dfrac{0.6}{0.6-\mathrm{P}} \\ 10^{4}=\dfrac{0.6}{0.6-\mathrm{P}} \\ \Rightarrow 0.6\times 10^{4}-10^{4}\mathrm{P}=0.6 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 10^{4}\mathrm{P}=0.6\left (10^{4}-1\right ) \\ \mathrm{P}=(6000-0.6)\times 10^{-4} \\ =5999.\times 10^{-4} \\ =0.59994 \\ \mathrm{P}_{\text{Total}}=0.6+\dfrac{\mathrm{P}}{2} \\ =0.6+0.29997 \\ =0.89997 \\ =899.97\times 10^{-3} \\ \text{Ans.}900 \end{array} \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\mathrm{P}_{\text{Total}}=0.6+\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2}$

As given in equation

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{r}}=4.606\times 10^{-2}\sec ^{-1}$

(Here language conflict in question)

($\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{\mathrm{KA}}{2}$ not considered)

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{t} & =\ln \dfrac{0.6}{0.6-\mathrm{x}} \\ 4.606 & \times 10^{-2}\times 100=2.303\log \dfrac{0.6}{0.6-\mathrm{x}} \\ \mathrm{P}_{\text{Total}} & =0.6+\dfrac{0.594}{2}=0.897\mathrm{atm} \\  & =897\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{atm} \end{array}$

text: The standard enthalpy and standard entropy of decomposition of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ to $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ are $55.0\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and $175.0\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{K}/\mathrm{mol}$ respectively. The standard free energy change for this reaction at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ in J $\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is $________ ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\circ }=55\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol},\mathrm{T}=298\mathrm{K}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=175\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{K}/\mathrm{mol} \\ \Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{T}\Delta \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}} \\ \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=55000\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol}-298\times 175\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol} \\ \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=55000-52150 \\ \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{rxn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=2850\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
If 1 mM solution of ethylamine produces $\mathrm{pH}=9$, then the ionization constant $(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}})$ of ethylamine is $10^{-x}$. The value of $x$ is $_________ ($nearest integer).

[The degree of ionization of ethylamine can be neglected with respect to unity.]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{2}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}⇌\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{3}^{+}+\mathrm{O}^{⊖}\mathrm{H}$

$\begin{array}{lll} \mathrm{C}=10^{-3}\mathrm{M} & - & - \\ \mathrm{C}(1-α) & \mathrm{C}α & \mathrm{C}α \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=10^{-3} & =10^{-5} & =10^{-5} \end{array}$

$1-α\simeq 1$

Given, $\mathrm{pH}=9\Rightarrow \mathrm{pOH}=5\Rightarrow [\mathrm{O}^{⊖}\mathrm{H}]=10^{-5}\mathrm{M}$

Now, $K_{b}=\frac{\left [\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{3}^{+}\right ][\mathrm{O}^{⊖}\mathrm{H}]}{[\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{2}]}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{10^{-5}\times 10^{-5}}{10^{-3}}=10^{-7}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift
